ANSWER_Q2_6: Table 3 gives C_M = C_R = 0 for both Blank and Copy-last, even though their 1x transformed E(5) errors are 0.0426 and 0.0641. Blank commutes with each transformation because transforming an all-zero image changes nothing. Copy-last commutes because selecting the last input frame and repeating it can be done before or after transforming the frames. Thus exact consistency tests whether a predictor respects the transformation, not whether it forecasts motion correctly. E_T must accompany C_T to distinguish an accurate equivariant forecast from a consistently wrong one.
ANSWER_Q2_7: For the mirror panel of video 9658 in Figure 3 (A, seed 0, 1x), compare rows 3 and 4 at h = 4 and 5. Starting from the identical mirrored inputs, direct prediction in row 3 draws the two digits together into a diffuse central patch by h = 5. Mirroring the original forecast in row 4 instead retains two displaced patches, with one above and to the right of the other. The difference is therefore in the forecast locations and merging of the digits, not just their reflected stroke shapes. The true future in row 2 shows the digits approaching and overlapping with recognisable strokes, so neither blurred account is a clean recovery of their motion and identity.
